- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.25), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After a price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 3–8% in subsequent periods.
- Model consistently underestimates prices in early periods of a downward trend; increase forecast by 1–3% if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment is high (≥ 0.5) and price is falling, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; adjust forecast upward by 1–4% to align with historical mean.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to sentiment shifts; if sentiment turns positive after a negative period, delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 periods.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overestimates near the end of the forecast window; cap forecast at 10% below the 30-day moving average of recent 10-day prices.
